title: Control plane API burst backpressure during private upgrade — mitigation & follow-up
creator: Marisol Chen
description: During a staged private control plane upgrade on 2026-02-09 we observed a correlated spike in management API traffic originating from upgraded control plane replicas. The burst overwhelmed etcd and internal admin proxies, causing transient 5xx responses and a subset of private clusters to lose control-plane heartbeat visibility for 3–12 minutes. This ticket tracks root cause analysis, short/medium-term mitigations implemented during the incident, and longer-term engineering work to prevent recurrence.
root_cause: A newly-introduced background reconciliation loop in the control plane (change in 2026-01) did not honor global rate limits when replicas started hot after upgrade. Multiple replicas simultaneously retried wide reconciliation windows (full-cluster object scans), producing an API burst pattern that exceeded etcd leader capacity and caused request queuing and timeouts. The control plane lacked a coordinated token-bucket and leader-aware backoff for this code path, and autoscaling thresholds for the admin proxy were too conservative for short-lived bursts.
action_items: ENG-46872-A1: Add per-replica token-bucket throttler + leader-aware gating to reconciliation worker (owner: Arjun Patel, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-08)
ENG-46872-A2: Implement exponential jittered backoff on full-cluster reconciles and add coalescing for identical workload keys (owner: Lena Soto, estimate: 5, due: 2026-03-15)
ENG-46872-A3: Change default admin-proxy HPA policy to include short-burst scaling (owner: Priya Desai, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-05)

ENG-46872-A4: Add telemetry (per-reconcile op counts, token-bucket occupancy, leader-elections) and Grafana runbook panels; create alert for sustained etcd leader queue latency (owner: Observability team, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-10)

ENG-46872-A5: Update private upgrade orchestration to serialize control-plane instance rollouts with a 90s inter-replica delay and health check gating (owner: Release Infra team, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-01)
ENG-46872-A6: Add unit+integration tests that simulate simultaneous reconcile starts and assert rate-limiter behavior (owner: QA, estimate: 4, due: 2026-03-20)

ENG-46872-A7: Revise runbook: communicate expected upgrade noise to SRE, add immediate mitigation steps (scale admin-proxy, pause rollouts, apply temporary leader pin) (owner: SRE, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-03)
notes: 2026-02-09 09:12 UTC — Incident detected: spike in control-plane 5xx errors across 18 private clusters. Pager duty triggered (oncall: Nana Okoye).

2026-02-09 09:25 UTC — Triage: whole-cluster reconciliation sweeps observed starting at 09:18 from multiple replicas; etcd leader latency increased. Short-term mitigation: scale admin-proxy + drain one replica to reduce simultaneous load. Immediate impact reduced to isolated clusters.
2026-02-09 11:00 UTC — Root-cause hypothesis formed: new reconcile worker code path lacks rate limiter. Ran controlled repro in staging: confirmed burst pattern and leader queue growth.

2026-02-10 14:40 UTC — Emergency patch deployed to add a global in-process token bucket limiting reconcile starts to 2/s across control plane replicas; observed stabilization in production. Patch rolled back into mainline with tests. (PR #3287)
2026-02-12 10:05 UTC — Post-incident meeting with SRE/Runtime/Release: agreed on action items list and prioritized token-bucket + orchestration changes. Assigned owners and dates in ticket.
2026-02-20 16:30 UTC — Design review for leader-aware gating and coalescing held. Feedback: ensure leader handover paths avoid deadlock; prefer eventualconsistency for non-critical resources.
2026-02-24 09:00 UTC — Observability team added dashboards for reconcile op counts and etcd leader queue depth; alert thresholds set at 95th percentile increase over 10m.
2026-03-01 12:30 UTC — Work in progress: Arjun opened PR to add token-bucket and leader-awareness; integration tests pending. Admin-proxy HPA change staged in canary pools.
